questions.question: Steapsin, the enzyme which converts fats into fatty acids and glycerol, is secreted by ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**pancreas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Steapsin** is also known as** pancreatic lipase**, which is a digestive enzyme that breaks down fats into fatty acids and glycerol.
 
• The stomach secretes hydrochloric acid and pepsin, which are responsible for breaking down proteins, while the small intestine secretes enzymes such as amylase, protease, and lipase for the breakdown of carbohydrates, proteins, and fats respectively.
 
• The large intestine is responsible for the absorption of water and electrolytes and the formation of feces.
 
• The pancreas is an important organ in the digestive system as it secretes several digestive enzymes such as pancreatic amylase, proteases, and lipases, which aid in the digestion and absorption of nutrients.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• The stomach is a muscular sac-like organ that is responsible for the initial breakdown of food through the process of mechanical and chemical digestion.
 
• The small intestine is a long tube-like organ that is responsible for the majority of nutrient absorption in the digestive system.
 
• The large intestine, also known as the colon, is a wider tube-like organ that absorbs water and electrolytes from undigested food and forms feces for elimination.
 
• Steapsin, also known as pancreatic lipase, is a crucial enzyme for the digestion of fats in the small intestine.
 
• The pancreas is an exocrine gland that secretes digestive enzymes into the small intestine and an endocrine gland that secretes hormones such as insulin and glucagon into the bloodstream.

questions.question: English East India Company acquired Diwani of Bengal in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1765**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The English East India Company **acquired the **Diwani of Bengal in 1765 **through the Treaty of Allahabad signed between the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II and the Company's representative, Robert Clive.
 
• The Diwani of Bengal refers to the right to collect revenue from the Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa regions. This was a significant acquisition for the English East India Company as it gave them control over a vast area and a significant source of revenue.
 
• In 1757, the English East India Company won the Battle of Plassey against the Nawab of Bengal, Siraj-ud-Daulah, which gave them control over Bengal. However, they did not acquire the Diwani until 1765.
 
• While the English East India Company had established its presence in Bengal by this time, they did not acquire the Diwani until 1765.
 
• By this time, the English East India Company had already acquired the Diwani of Bengal and had been collecting revenue from the region for five years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• From 1600 to 1874, the English East India Company (EIC) operated as a joint-stock business, engaging in trade in the Indian Ocean area.
 
• The company's purpose was to take advantage of trade with India, East and Southeast Asia, and to enable England to trade in East Indian spices.
 
• Later, the EIC acquired and ruled over land, establishing trading factories in India and other Asian countries.
 
• The British Crown annexed the lands of the EIC in the middle of the 19th century and included them in the British Empire.

questions.question: As a result of which act did Queen Victoria, who was the monarch of Britain, also became the sovereign of British territories in India, with the title "Empress of India" in 1858?

• **The Indian Councils Act of 1861** was passed to allow for the addition of Indian members to the legislative councils in India.
 
• This act did not result in Queen Victoria becoming the Empress of India.
 
• The act did, however, provide for greater Indian representation in the government of India.
 
• **The Charter Act of 1833 **was passed to abolish the East India Company's monopoly on trade with India.
 
• This act did not result in Queen Victoria becoming the Empress of India.
 
• The act did, however, provide for some limited Indian representation in the government of India.
 
• **The Regulating Act of 1773 **was passed to establish British control over the East India Company.
 
• This act did not result in Queen Victoria becoming the Empress of India.
 
• The act did, however, provide for greater British oversight of the East India Company's activities in India.

questions.question: When was the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana launched by the Government of India?

questions.question: Which among the following is a subject of the State List in the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Agriculture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Indian Constitution** divides the** legislative powers between the Centre and the States**. The State List contains 61 subjects over which the State Legislatures have exclusive power to legislate.
 
• Agriculture is one of the subjects included in the State List. This means that the State Governments have the power to make laws and policies related to agriculture within their respective states.
 
• Banking is a subject that falls under the Union List, which means that the Central Government has the power to legislate on matters related to banking. However, cooperative banks and regional rural banks come under the purview of both the Centre and the States.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ports are also a subject that falls under the Union List, which means that the Central Government has the power to legislate on matters related to ports. However, the State Governments can also make laws and policies related to minor ports within their respective states.
 
• Railways are a subject that falls under the Union List.

questions.question: Major plantations are found in the ______ region of the world.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tropical**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tropical regions** are characterized by a hot and humid climate, which is ideal for the growth of various crops and plantations. Hence, major plantations are found in tropical regions.
 
• The tropical region extends between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn, which includes countries such as Brazil, Indonesia, India, and Nigeria, among others.
 
• Parts of **North America, South America, Africa, Asia, and Australia** are included in the tropics, as is the Equator. Approximately one-third of the global population resides in the tropics, which make up 36% of the planet's landmass.
 
• Tropical temperatures range from 25 to 28 degrees Celsius (77 to 82 degrees Fahrenheit) on average throughout the year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Plantations in tropical regions are mainly focused on crops such as coffee, tea, cocoa, bananas, rubber, palm oil, and sugar cane, among others.
 
• Apart from the tropical region, plantations are also found in other regions of the world, such as grasslands, temperate regions, and deserts, but they are not as extensive as those found in tropical regions.
 
• Grasslands are characterized by a moderate climate and are mainly used for grazing livestock. Temperate regions have a moderate climate and are used for crops such as wheat, corn, and soybeans. Deserts have a hot and dry climate and are mainly used for crops such as dates, figs, and olives.
